key_insight: Zeroth-order gradient reliability hinges on data matching: mismatched evaluations amplify oracle noise as 1/μ², while matched evaluations cancel this amplification.
engineering_relevance: ZO-BOLT offers a route to RLVR-aligned LLM post-training with more reliable gradient estimates and a near-inference memory footprint.
method: Analyze matched versus mismatched finite-difference evaluations through a variance-theoretic framework.
Derive convergence guarantees with explicit constants separating the two regimes.
Build ZO-BOLT on Boltzmann Targeted SFT's matched-data advantage.
evidence_signal: Perturbation-scale sweeps and matched-versus-mismatched comparisons support the theory; experiments across three models and two mathematical reasoning benchmarks show consistent gains over pretrained baselines.
watch_item: The abstract reports limited model and benchmark coverage; cancelling mismatch-induced amplification does not establish noise-free optimization.
paper_title: The Cost of Mismatch: Noise Amplification in Zeroth-Order Reinforcement Learning
